mouth.method: aimed by hand in the viewer's mouth editor (docs/triassic/mouths/cartorhynchus-mouth.json); the modelled cavity -- a shallow groove, 26 vertices on the snout against 193 on Placodus -- is measured beside it and no longer cuts
mouth.note: The cut is aimed by hand and no longer measured. Placodus' geometric method returns 63 vertices over the whole front third and only 26 of them on the rostrum -- one band two thousandths deep, which is the lip this generation drew rather than the joint its jaw turns about. A reviewer aimed the plane and the hinge on the shipped body in the viewer's mouth editor; the groove is still measured, and what the two disagree about is in mouthCutDeviation.
mouth.oralGeometry: none: the cut is capped with its own rim and domed into each half (T.cap_cut at the hinge cross-section, then T.cap_mouth along the mouth line), and the closed sac lining and the seated hinge ellipsoid this body shipped with are gone

skinTears.note: The lining wall is built to stretch -- roof on the skull, floor on the jaw -- so its ratio at full gape says the mouth opened, not that anything tore. `skin` is the figure to compare against the shore batch's (Nothosaurus 2.98x, Tanystropheus 6.1x, Placodus 12.4x).
